tone 3 white noise LPF, T1 0, T3 5-10, L3 0
tone 1 small NEGATIVE while lfo_depth_tvf small positive
steps.why: inverted tremolo keeps the loudness steady

performance.why: pan pipe players bend a lot

recipes.name: Recorder / penny whistle
recipes.summary: A dominant fundamental and a weak 2nd harmonic: a ~40 % pulse (woody with some edge) or a quiet triangle. The filter envelope peaks before the amplitude (a bright chiff while the note is still rising), a note-off 'thunk' from a set release, a tiny random brightness wander, no vibrato. Best from middle C up two octaves.
pitfalls: Pitch vibrato sounds wrong on recorder.

steps.why: the amp slower than the filter; release = thunk

steps.set: RND, slow, tiny TVF depth; pitch depth 0

recipes.name: Clarinet-like woodwind
recipes.summary: A closed cylindrical pipe with a reed gives odd harmonics only: a square wave, 'hollow'. Mellow LPF, a moderate attack, delayed gentle vibrato.

recipes.name: Oboe / reedy double-reed
recipes.summary: Thin and nasal: a narrow pulse (5-15 %) or oboe PCM, a moderately open filter, delayed vibrato.

recipes.name: Tonewheel drawbar organ (unadorned)
recipes.summary: A Hammond is additive: sine partials at 16' (-12), 5 1/3' (+7), 8' (0), 4' (+12), 2 2/3' (+19), 2' (+24), 1 3/5' (+28), 1 1/3' (+31) and 1' (+36), with drawbar levels. 88 8000 000 = the classic punchy registration. Rectangular envelope, key-click, no velocity, precise tuning.
pitfalls: Filter resonance or extra harmonics (5th, 7th) make it too bright.
Velocity sensitivity makes it un-organ-like.

steps.set: Sine on up to 4 tones (or organ PCM 30/258-281 for full registrations)

performance.set: optional tiny fast blip on one tone

recipes.name: Full Hammond: percussion, scanner chorus, overdrive, Leslie
recipes.summary: The Hammond sound = tonewheels + percussion (a decaying 2nd or 3rd harmonic accent) + scanner chorus (C-3: dry + one vibrato'd copy, ~6-7 Hz) + valve overdrive (with chord compression) + the Leslie (horn and rotor above/below 800 Hz, separate speeds, audible acceleration, Doppler about +-1 %, tremolo 90 deg out of phase, reflections). Chain: organ -> drive -> rotary -> cabinet.
pitfalls: Multi-stage ensemble chorus is too lush for Hammond scanner chorus.
Pure V (vibrato) settings sound cheesy to many players.

steps.set: organ PCM (VK 259-263, Jazz 271/275) or sine drawbars (organ.drawbar)
percussion tone: T1 0, T3 20-30 (fast) or 40-60 (slow), L3 0, NO-SUS
Org Click on a short tone, low level

effects.set: VK ROTARY (drive + rotary; woofer/tweeter speeds and rise/fall times)

recipes.name: Acoustic grand piano
recipes.summary: Only samples convince. Keep the wave's attack; crossfade soft/loud layers by velocity; harder = brighter; high notes brighter but shorter and quieter; a two-slope decay; stretch tuning; sustain pedal with sympathetic resonance; no chorus, no LFO, no bend; a hall/room.
pitfalls: Reshaping the PCM attack with the envelope ruins the hammer transient.
Chorus or LFO on an acoustic piano sounds cheap.

steps.why: the Editor manual: good for acoustic piano

effects.why: chorus is wrong for acoustic piano

recipes.summary: Subtractive 'pianos' end up Rhodes/Wurlitzer-like, which is valuable in itself. The JX10 recipe: a wiry synced tone with a big timbral blip at the attack (the hammer), a plain square body that takes over in the decay, a piano-shaped envelope (instant attack, long decay, no sustain), key-follow shortening, a modest velocity-scaled filter envelope, no chorus/LFO. effects.why: the amp and speaker are the sound

recipes.name: Acoustic / nylon guitar
recipes.summary: Acoustic guitars can't be synthesized subtractively; use PCM with velocity layers. Harder pluck = brighter and longer (Matrix VELOCITY -> TVA decay), a two-slope decay, the filter following the amp, and shorter decays at high notes. Mono for single-string lines.

recipes.name: Classic analogue synth bass / bass guitar imitation
recipes.summary: Synth Secrets notes that saw + pulse together give remarkably accurate bass-guitar imitations; saw + square an octave down gives body. Punchy: instant attack, a filter envelope spike, multi-trigger. Fat: detuned layers or unison.

30-50, env +30...+50 fast decay, resonance to taste
T1 0; sustain medium-high for synth, 0 for plucked bass

recipes.name: 808-style kick (boom)
recipes.summary: A pinged, self-decaying sine with a small pitch drop that goes slightly flat on long decays, plus a trigger click tamed by an LPF. Boom length = decay.
pitfalls: Avoid an unintended click on smooth kicks: T1 not exactly 0 if clicky.

recipes.name: 909-style kick (punchy)
recipes.summary: A near-sine body with a bigger, faster pitch drop, plus low-passed noise and a click pulse with their own short envelopes. Tight = short decay + fast drop.

steps.set: tone 1 T3 short-medium; tone 2 (232 noise, LPF cutoff 60-80) T3 10-20; tone 3 (248 click) T3 ~0-5

recipes.name: Snare drum (analogue-style)
recipes.summary: A tonal body (0,1 modes ~180 Hz and ~330 Hz, the upper decaying faster) plus snare-wire noise. Velocity moves the balance from tonal to noisy and brightens it. Simple version: full noise, LPF fully open, no resonance, a short decay, retrigger on every hit for rolls.

recipes.name: Hi-hats, ride and crash cymbals (metal)
recipes.summary: A dense, flat, inharmonic fog. The best affordable method is several pairs of ring/FM-modulated square waves at unrelated pitches (Korg Rhythm 55), band-split with different decays (highs shortest). Crash/ride: a mid 'ping' sweeping down to ~1 kHz over 0.2 s plus a high-passed tail opening upward over 0.2 s and closing slowly. Hats = short decays; open hat = longer.
pitfalls: Noise alone gives a 'weedy' synthetic cymbal.
A low filter ceiling kills cymbals: keep the cutoff high.

steps.set: closed hat T3 5-10; open 40-60; ride 40-60 with NO-SUS

performance.set: MONO with open and closed hats in one patch

recipes.name: 808/CR-8000 cowbell
recipes.summary: Two triangles at 587 Hz and 845 Hz (ratio 1:1.44), the upper slightly louder, band-pass ~2.6 kHz (12 dB) with slight resonance, a two-stage decay (a loud short impact, then a tail), and a faint pink-noise halo. Exact tuning matters.
pitfalls: Small tuning deviations destroy the cowbell illusion.

steps.set: Syn Triangle on tones 1+2; play D5
L1 127, L2 50-60, L3 0 (T2 very short, T3 medium)
optional tone 3 Pink Noise, very short, low

recipes.name: Claves / woodblock
recipes.summary: A triangle through a band-pass with no resonance and a very short decay: a woody click. PCM 139 JD Wood Crak / 142 JD Log Drum are alternatives.

recipes.name: Timpani (kettle drum)
recipes.summary: Four sine partials at 1.00 : 1.50 : 1.98 : 2.44 of the principal (~150 Hz), amplitudes ~5:4:3:1, relative decays ~45/73/91/84 %, plus a short enharmonic strike burst (tuned rough pink noise or ring mod). Velocity sets only the level. Play pitch with the bend (+-a fifth).

recipes.name: Church / tubular / hand bell
recipes.summary: Three phases: a fast inharmonic strike (clang); a strike note of a few strong, slightly stretched low partials (a 2:3:4 pattern implies the pitch); a long sub-octave hum that beats slowly. Warble from nearly identical modes beating. Needs a reverb.

steps.set: Tubular Bell / 155 Church Bell as the quick route
synth: tone 1 sine + FXM 4-8, color 1-2; decay two-stage
tone 2 +12 with +15...+30 ct (stretched); tone 3 -12 (hum); tone 4 -12 +2...+4 ct (beating)

recipes.name: Metallic / clangorous percussion and FX
recipes.summary: Inharmonic partials: ring mod between tones at odd ratios (a fixed-pitch modulator = the timbre changes across the keyboard), FXM with low colour, FM-style envelopes on the index, short percussive envelopes.

steps.set: TYPE 05-10; tone 2 at an odd interval (+6, +11, +13 with odd cents)
modulator tone 0 for an enharmonic keyboard sweep; 100 for a consistent timbre

recipes.name: Classic mono synth lead
recipes.summary: Saw (or square for hollow), a resonant LPF with a punchy envelope spike, mono with a chosen trigger mode (legato slurs vs multi-trigger punch), portamento, delayed vibrato on the mod bar, bend. Fat = detuned unison layers.

performance.set: ON for singing lines, OFF for punchy staccato
CC01 -> LFO1 PCH DEPTH; AFTERTOUCH -> CUTOFF or LFO TVF DEPTH (growl)

recipes.name: 'Sync' lead (tearing timbre sweep)
recipes.summary: Hard sync sweeps timbre, not pitch, as the slave's pitch is swept by an envelope. The AX-Synth has no oscillator sync: use the 219 Sync Sweep PCM, or FXM with the TVF envelope routed to FXM DEPTH for an evolving harmonic sweep.

steps.set: alternative: FXM ON on a saw; Matrix TVF ENV -> FXM DEPTH +

recipes.name: Warm pad ('carpet')
recipes.summary: Detuned saws or pad PCM, a moderate LPF with slow movement (slow LFO or a long filter envelope), a slow attack and long release, no velocity, chorus + a hall. Evolving: layers with different envelopes crossfading.

steps.set: 124 Warm Pad / 125-126 OB2 Pad / 127 D-50 Heaven / detuned saws

recipes.name: Choir / vocal / formant sound
recipes.summary: Vowels are fixed formant peaks (ee 270/2300/3000 Hz, oo 300/870/2250, a 660/1700/2400 for an adult male; women's slightly higher/wider). Use choir or formant PCM or a HUMANIZER vowel filter; a slow attack, a little vibrato, chorus and hall. The AX-Synth has no vocoder/audio input.
pitfalls: Don't promise vocoder sounds: there's no audio input.

steps.set: Female Ahs (132 Oos, 133 Male Aahs, 234-238 formant waves)
